title: Indian foreign secretary to visit Nepal ahead of Balendra Shah’s proposed India trip - The Kathmandu Post
description: Indian foreign secretary to visit Nepal ahead of Balendra Shah’s proposed India trip  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal and India on Monday announced that Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri would visit Kathmandu on November 4-5, as the two neighbours seek to strengthen ties and review key areas of cooperation.

According to Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Misri is visiting at the invitation of his Nepali counterpart, Amrit Bahadur Rai. The two foreign secretaries will review the full range of Nepal-India relations and exchange views on matters of mutual interest.

Misri will also discuss bilateral, regional and global issues of common interest, according to a statement issued by India’s Ministry of External Affairs.

He is scheduled to pay courtesy calls on senior Nepali officials and political leaders before returning to New Delhi on November 5. He is also expected to meet Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

The visit comes as Kathmandu and New Delhi prepare for Shah’s proposed official visit to India, expected in the second half of November. Although the dates have yet to be announced, the two sides have stepped up diplomatic engagement to prepare for the visit and identify areas for cooperation.

Misri’s visit is expected to provide an opportunity to discuss the agenda, priorities and possible outcomes of Shah’s trip, as well as broader bilateral relations. The two sides are also likely to discuss issues that could feature prominently in talks between the prime ministers.

“India and Nepal share strong and friendly ties which have seen substantial progress across diverse areas of cooperation. The Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” the Indian statement said.

The proposed trip would be Shah’s first official bilateral visit abroad since he took office on March 27. India extended an invitation to him soon after his government was formed. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has said both countries are working to make the visit productive and result-oriented, with a focus on advancing cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

Nepal and India maintain a broad relationship covering trade, transit, investment, energy, connectivity, security and people-to-people exchanges. India is Nepal’s largest trading partner and a major source of foreign investment. Bilateral merchandise trade stood at approximately $9.38 billion in the 2025-26 fiscal year, accounting for more than 60 percent of Nepal’s total external goods trade.

The two countries have more than 40 bilateral institutional mechanisms dealing with various aspects of their relationship, including border management, trade, security, water resources, hydropower and connectivity.

The foreign secretary-level talks follow Khanal’s official visit to India in June, when he met Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. The two ministers reviewed cooperation in development partnership, connectivity, trade and transit, energy and people-to-people relations. They also discussed regional and multilateral issues and agreed to step up cooperation in emerging areas, including digital and financial technology, innovation and capacity building.

The upcoming diplomatic engagement is also expected to take place against the backdrop of longstanding bilateral issues, including border disputes, trade and transit arrangements, cross-border connectivity and the implementation of existing agreements.

title: Nepal Initiates Process to Merge LP Gas Industries - Ratopati
description: Nepal Initiates Process to Merge LP Gas Industries  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. The process of merging LP gas industries operating in Nepal has been initiated. The Nepal Oil Corporation has moved forward with the implementation of the policy to merge gas industries operating under various names and brands, in accordance with point number 32 of the approved policy and program for the current fiscal year 2083/084.

In this regard, the corporation had sent letters to all gas industries on November 12, encouraging the policy of merging and requesting them to move forward with the process by creating an action plan accordingly.

The corporation expects that merging gas industries will further systematize and facilitate the sales and distribution system. The corporation believes this will also ease gas supply and distribution for consumers.

title: Students gather in worship, fundraise for flood relief in Nepal - Calvin University Chimes
description: Students gather in worship, fundraise for flood relief in Nepal  Calvin University Chimes
publisher.title: Calvin University Chimes
full_article:
On Friday, Oct. 30, students and community members came together in the Hekman Library basement to support victims of the recent flood caused by a glacial collapse in Nepal. The event, Gather for Nepal, featured worship, prayer, food and wares organized by Nepali students at Calvin, with funds raised going to support relief efforts.

The event opened with prayer from Campus Pastor Mary Hulst and an address from Calvin University President Greg Elzinga, followed by a presentation from the student organizers about the devastation caused by the flooding.

On Aug. 26, flash floods swept through Nepal, displacing entire communities. According to the United Nations , more than 1,500 people lost their lives in the flood, and 5,600 remain missing. According to the students’ presentation, 22,000 children lack access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene.

The evening was rounded out by worship, songs and prayer led by students in both English and Nepali.

One student in attendance, senior Anna Malaker, told Chimes, “It was just a great opportunity to witness the Calvin community come together for something that we care about … we’re raising money for such a good cause, but also wanting to lift up all those families affected in prayer.” She continued, “I personally have had family affected by similar things, and I think it means a lot to show up for your fellow classmates and peers to be able to show your love and support for them.”

Nischayata Byshunke, a junior Calvin student from Nepal and one of the event’s organizers, told Chimes how she has seen the Calvin community come together. “Having all the people actually be there and be like, ‘hey, we’re with you, supporting you’ … Calvin feels a bit more like home to me now,” said Byshunke.

According to Charchit Adhikari, another student organizer, the support coming from the Calvin community goes a long way toward helping those in Nepal, with the group focusing support on helping displaced families. “If I send a dollar from here, it’s worth so much, about 150 rupees,” said Adhikari. “If we can just collect a few thousand dollars, that will help us make … a safer space for the children.”

The student organizers partnered with Student Senate to put on the event at Calvin, with all funds raised through donations, food sales and a quilt auction going towards relief efforts by Higher Ground Nepal.

Higher Ground Nepal was founded by Calvin alumna Bimala Shrestha Pokharel, who addressed the gathering through a video documenting the site where funds raised by the Calvin students are already being put to work constructing bathrooms, showers and sanitation facilities in the municipality of Godawari.

“Through your generous support, we are in the process of giving bathrooms and shower rooms for children affected by flood,” said Pokharel in her video, sharing, “on behalf of Higher Ground Nepal … we appreciate your prayers and support. Thank you so much.”

The group’s first fundraiser on Oct. 9 raised half of their $4,200 goal. Adhikari credited the community with the success of the fundraising efforts, saying, “Every organization, every Instagram page, Calvin CISD, Knightlife, they have all been partnering with us for the posts and Instagram, and that helped us reach out to so many people.” Adhikari said, “None of us had ever thought we will get that kind of support from the students, from the staff, from the faculty; everyone was there.”

title: US overtakes India as Nepal’s largest tourism source market for first time - The Kathmandu Post
description: US overtakes India as Nepal’s largest tourism source market for first time  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Arrivals from the United States have overtaken those from India to become Nepal’s largest source of foreign tourists for the first time, as a sharp decline in Indian visitors amid the fallout from the August floods reshaped the country’s tourism market in October.

Nepal received 17,437 American tourists in October, a 31.24 percent increase from the same month last year, according to data released by the Nepal Tourism Board, the country’s tourism promotion agency. The number more than doubled from September, when 8,299 Americans visited Nepal.

India, traditionally Nepal’s largest tourism source market, slipped to second place. The country received 12,097 Indian visitors in October, down 30 percent from the same month last year. The number was also significantly lower than September’s 17,425.

China ranked third, with 11,695 visitors in October, a 73 percent increase from the same month last year. In September, Nepal received 11,212 Chinese tourists.

The shift comes despite the devastating August 26 floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems, which generated negative international publicity and triggered a wave of cancellations across Nepal’s hospitality industry.

Nepal received 132,814 foreign tourists in October, a 3.4 percent increase from the same month last year. The recovery followed a sharp decline in September, when the disaster’s immediate aftermath disrupted travel plans and prompted cancellations. In August, Nepal had received 88,248 foreign visitors.

“This is the first time in history that arrivals from the US have topped Nepal’s tourism source markets, and it is encouraging news for the industry,” said Mani Raj Lamichhane, director at the Nepal Tourism Board. “The arrivals from the US to take the top spot is mainly due to the decline in Indian tourists.”

The floods and landslides have also had a devastating human toll, with hundreds of foreign nationals among those reported missing. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 636 foreigners have been reported missing, most of them non-resident Indians travelling to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage through Nepal.

The disaster has so far claimed 1,451 lives, while 5,745 people remain missing.

Despite the scale of the devastation and the circulation of distressing images and videos, American travellers appear to have remained largely undeterred.

Ganga Bahadur Thapa, managing director of Nepal Hiking Team, which primarily caters to American travellers, said the company had not received a single cancellation following the disaster. A few clients postponed their trips, but most continued with their plans.

“In fact, we didn’t receive a single cancellation. Only a few postponed their trips,” said Thapa, whose company handles more than 1,200 American travellers annually.

Courtesy of Nepal Tourism Board

According to Thapa, American tourists tend to assess ground realities before making travel decisions rather than relying solely on headlines and travel advisories.

“The August 26 disaster affected the popular Langtang trekking region, but other areas were safe, and they knew that,” he said.

Tour operators say Nepal has also been attracting younger American travellers interested in adventure activities, including trekking and mountaineering.

When the disaster struck, Thapa’s company offered clients who had booked Langtang treks alternative itineraries, including the Annapurna Circuit and Everest Base Camp routes, without increasing the cost.

“When the disaster struck, we gave our clients who had booked Langtang treks several options, such as the Annapurna Circuit and Everest Base Camp treks, without inflating the costs, and they were convinced. That is why we did not receive a single cancellation,” he said.

Pawan Tuladhar, founder and owner of Dharma Adventures, another tour operator popular among American travellers, said the US had long been a reliable market for Nepal, despite limited promotional activities targeting American tourists.

“The American market has always been reliable for Nepal. They are a high-end segment and have been growing consistently over the past years,” he said.

Tuladhar said the expansion of American hotel chains in Nepal had also helped build confidence among travellers by providing familiar accommodation options and international service standards.

“The rise in American tourists, who are among the highest spenders in the world, is definitely good news for Nepal’s tourism industry,” he said.

Some operators also attribute part of the increase to the growing Nepali diaspora in the United States. Nepalis holding American passports increasingly visit their homeland, particularly during major festivals such as Dashain and Tihar.

But tourism entrepreneurs say the main reason Americans emerged as Nepal’s largest source market in October was not simply the growth in US arrivals. It was also the sharp contraction in Indian travel following the August disaster.

Bimal Naharki, president of the Association of Kailash Tour Operators Nepal, said more than 5,000 Indian pilgrims had cancelled their Kailash Mansarovar trips scheduled for September after the floods.

“As roads collapsed and transportation was disrupted, it affected Indian tourists’ travel plans for October as well,” he said.

The Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage is a lucrative business for Nepali tour operators, generating substantial economic activity across the tourism, aviation and hospitality sectors.

Nepali operators routinely handle tens of thousands of Indian and non-resident Indian pilgrims each season, with quotas and travel arrangements often involving 24,000 to 25,000 visitors. The pilgrimage supports hotels, restaurants and guest houses in gateway cities such as Nepalgunj and mountain hubs such as Simkot in Humla. It also provides work for local guides, porters and drivers.

The Nepal route, through overland crossings such as Kerung or flights and helicopter transfers via Simkot and Hilsa, is considered one of the more accessible and cost-effective ways to reach Tibet.

The disruption of these routes has therefore affected more than pilgrimage operators. It has also hit businesses across the wider tourism supply chain.

Tour operators say Indian travellers tend to be particularly sensitive to safety concerns and disruptions to transport infrastructure. Many travel in large family groups or on religious pilgrimages, making reliable road access, group accommodation, vegetarian food and other family-friendly services important considerations.

Unlike some independent travellers who may be willing to change destinations or itineraries at short notice, organised pilgrimage groups often depend on fixed schedules and coordinated transport arrangements. Operators say it could take months for Indian arrivals to recover as travellers wait for reassurance that Nepal’s roads and tourism destinations are safe.

The latest decline is a setback for an industry that had begun to see a strong recovery in its largest traditional source market.

In 2023, following the Covid pandemic, Nepal received 319,936 Indian tourists through air routes, the highest annual figure on record. But a series of natural disasters and other disruptions in 2024 caused Indian arrivals to decline for several consecutive months.

After months of fluctuations caused by political tensions, natural disasters, air crashes and rising airfares, Indian tourists had begun returning in record numbers, raising hopes of a sustained recovery.

In May this year, Nepal received 40,782 Indian visitors by air, the highest monthly number ever recorded, according to the Nepal Tourism Board. The figure represented a 32.66 percent increase from the same month last year and signalled a strong turnaround in Nepal’s biggest tourism source market.

title: Nepal keen to collaborate with Switzerland in climate change issues, says President Paudel - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal keen to collaborate with Switzerland in climate change issues, says President Paudel  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nov 2: President Ramchandra Paudel has stated that Nepal is keen to collaborate with Switzerland to address climate change and environmental challenges in the Himalayan region.

During a meeting today with a delegation led by President of the National Council of Switzerland, Pierre-André Page at the Office of the President, President Paudel emphasized Nepal's readiness to cooperate in mitigating the impacts of climate change.

He also appreciated the long-standing support Switzerland has extended toward strengthening Nepal’s democracy, federalism, local governance, and socio-economic development," according to the Office of the President.

President Paudel remarked that he has long been inspired by Switzerland’s robust democratic values and principles.

During the meeting, President of the Swiss National Council, Pierre-André Page noted that the Himalayas are becoming increasingly unstable, while underscoring the critical importance of early warning systems. He mentioned that Switzerland is already working in this area and expressed readiness to collaborate with Nepal towards that end. (RSS)
